body.statement: For every \(W\in\mathcal R_q\), the algorithm \(\mathsf{Enum}(W)\) emits every member of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{stab}}(W)\) exactly once. If \(c=|C|\) and \(e_C\) is the number of admissibility edges in block \(C\), its local screening time is \(\sum_C O((c^{1/2}e_C+cN_{\mathrm{adm}}(W_C))\operatorname{poly}(c,L))\), after which Cartesian-product output has \(O(q)\) delay per stable assignment. The claim is output-sensitive in the enumerated local matching fibers and does not assert polynomial delay in \(N_{\mathrm{stab}}(W)\) alone.
body.justification: The bound makes the positive algorithmic content exact without hiding rejected local matchings behind a polynomial-delay claim.
body.gap: Uno enumerates unfiltered perfect matchings, while prior local causal discovery does not integrate normalized Schur screening or SCC products.
body.consumer: The procedure is an exact fallback for stable matching frequencies when the largest feedback SCC is small.
body.proof_tex:
Let \(W\in\mathcal R_q\).  By \(\mathrm{def:rational\mbox{-}input\mbox{-}class}\), the four assumptions appearing in that definition hold.  In particular, \(B=I_q-W\) has rational entries by \(\mathrm{ass:rational\mbox{-}input}\).  Equality of a rational number to zero is decidable by inspecting its reduced numerator, so the directed support graph of \(B\) is computed exactly in time polynomial in \(q\) and \(L\).  From each vertex, a graph search computes the set of reachable vertices.  Mutual reachability is an equivalence relation, and its equivalence classes are exactly the strongly connected components.  Thus the first step of \(\mathsf{Enum}(W)\) computes \(\operatorname{SCC}(B)\) exactly, with polynomial bit complexity.

Fix a topological order of the condensation graph and let \(C\in\operatorname{SCC}(B)\), \(c=|C|\), and \(B_C=B[C,C]\).  In this order, both \(B\) and \(W=I_q-B\) are block triangular with diagonal blocks \(B_C\) and \(W_C=I_c-B_C\), respectively.  Therefore
\[
 \det(tI_q-B)=\prod_{D\in\operatorname{SCC}(B)}\det(tI_{|D|}-B_D)
 \quad\text{and}\quad
 \det(W)=\prod_{D\in\operatorname{SCC}(B)}\det(W_D).
\]
Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:stable\mbox{-}reference}\) gives \(\rho(B)<1\), so the first factorization implies \(\rho(B_C)<1\).  Assumption \(\mathrm{ass:invertible\mbox{-}equations}\) and the second factorization imply \(\det(W_C)\neq0\).  Rationality and its encoding-length bound pass from \(W\) to a principal submatrix by \(\mathrm{ass:rational\mbox{-}input}\), and \((W_C)_{ii}=1\) follows from \(\mathrm{ass:unit\mbox{-}diagonal}\).  Hence \(W_C\in\mathcal R_c\).  Notice also that the unit diagonal gives at least \(c\) nonzero entries in \(W_C\).

Let \(H_C\) be the bipartite graph having a column copy and a row copy of \(C\), with an edge from column \(i\) to row \(r\) precisely when \((W_C)_{ri}\neq0\), and let \(e_C\) be its number of edges.  A perfect matching of \(H_C\) is a bijection \(i\mapsto\pi_C(i)\) satisfying
\[
 (W_C)_{\pi_C(i),i}\neq0\qquad(i\in C).
\]
By \(\mathrm{def:admissible\mbox{-}orbit}\), these bijections are exactly the elements of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{adm}}(W_C)\).  Thus it remains to show that the matching recursion in \(\mathrm{def:local\mbox{-}enumerator}\) lists this finite set exactly once within the asserted bound.

Order the columns and, for each column, its incident rows.  At a prefix that injectively assigns the first \(k\) columns, consider each available incident row in order and recurse precisely when the residual bipartite graph has a perfect matching.  Residual feasibility is decided as follows.  Starting from any matching, search for an alternating path from an unmatched column to an unmatched row.  Flipping the edges along such a path increases the matching size by one.  If no such path exists while a column remains unmatched, let \(D\) be the set of columns reachable from all unmatched columns by alternating paths and let \(R\) be the reachable rows.  Every neighbor of \(D\) belongs to \(R\); every row in \(R\) is matched, since otherwise there would be an augmenting path; and following its matched edge maps \(R\) injectively into \(D\).  The image omits every initially unmatched column, so
\[
 |N(D)|=|R|<|D|.
\]
No matching can cover \(D\), because distinct columns would require distinct rows in \(N(D)\).  Consequently the residual graph has a perfect matching if and only if the augmentation process matches every residual column.  At most \(c\) augmentations are made, and each alternating search scans at most \(e_C\) edges, so one feasibility test costs \(O(ce_C)\) elementary graph operations.

Every perfect matching determines a unique root-to-leaf sequence of ordered prefix choices, and every reached leaf is a perfect matching because its prefixes passed the exact feasibility test.  Thus the recursion emits every member of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{adm}}(W_C)\) exactly once.  It is also an alternating-cycle recursion in the stated sense: the symmetric difference of two perfect matchings has degree zero or two at every vertex and hence is a disjoint union of even cycles whose edges alternate between the two matchings; the ordered branching chooses the first such differing edge.

Write \(N_C^{\mathrm{adm}}=N_{\mathrm{adm}}(W_C)\).  Associate to each feasible prefix its lexicographically least perfect-matching extension.  For a fixed perfect matching and a fixed depth there is at most one prefix having that matching as its extension, because a matching has only one prefix of that depth.  There are \(c+1\) depths, and therefore at most \((c+1)N_C^{\mathrm{adm}}\) feasible prefixes.  Each such prefix tests at most \(c\) candidate children.  If the root is infeasible, only its initial feasibility test is needed.  Since \(e_C\le c^2\), all powers of \(c\) and every factor \(e_C\) arising in these child tests can be absorbed into \(\operatorname{poly}(c,L)\).  The initial \(O(ce_C)\) cost can likewise be written as \(c^{1/2}e_C\operatorname{poly}(c,L)\).  Constructing \(H_C\) is covered by the same term because \(e_C\ge c\).  Hence exact-once enumeration of all local admissible matchings costs
\[
 O\!\left(\bigl(c^{1/2}e_C+cN_{\mathrm{adm}}(W_C)\bigr)
          \operatorname{poly}(c,L)\right).
\]

We next prove that the Schur screening required by \(\mathrm{def:local\mbox{-}enumerator}\) is exact.  For an admissible \(\pi_C\), \(\mathrm{def:normalized\mbox{-}candidate}\) gives the rational matrix
\[
 A=B_{\pi_C}
 =I_c-
   \operatorname{diag}\!\left((W_C)_{\pi_C(i),i}^{-1}:i\in C\right)
   P_{\pi_C}W_C.
\]
Every displayed divisor is nonzero by admissibility.  Thus the entries of \(A\) have binary length polynomial in \(c\) and \(L\).  Consider the \(c^2\)-variable rational linear system
\[
 P-A^{\mathsf T}PA=I_c. \tag{1}
\]
If \(\rho(A)<1\), then \(A^k\) converges geometrically to zero after putting \(A\) in complex Jordan form, and hence the series
\[
 P_\star=\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}(A^k)^{\mathsf T}A^k
\]
converges entrywise.  Shifting its index proves
\[
 P_\star-A^{\mathsf T}P_\star A=I_c.
\]
For every nonzero real vector \(x\), its \(k=0\) summand yields
\[
 x^{\mathsf T}P_\star x
 =\sum_{k=0}^{\infty}\lVert A^kx\rVert_2^2
 \geq \lVert x\rVert_2^2>0,
\]
so \(P_\star\) is positive definite.  The solution is unique: if \(H=A^{\mathsf T}HA\), iteration gives
\[
 H=(A^k)^{\mathsf T}HA^k\longrightarrow0,
\]
and therefore \(H=0\).

Conversely, suppose that a real symmetric positive-definite matrix \(P\) solves (1).  For any complex eigenpair \(Av=\lambda v\) with \(v\neq0\), extending the real quadratic form sesquilinearly gives
\[
 (1-|\lambda|^2)v^*Pv
 =v^*(P-A^{\mathsf T}PA)v
 =v^*v>0.
\]
Because \(v^*Pv>0\), this identity implies \(|\lambda|<1\).  It holds for every eigenvalue, so \(\rho(A)<1\).  We have proved the exact equivalence
\[
 \rho(A)<1
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \text{system (1) has a positive-definite solution}. \tag{2}
\]
In particular, (2) rejects the boundary \(\rho(A)=1\).

Fraction-free rational elimination decides whether (1) has a unique solution and computes it when it does.  If the system is singular, it may be rejected without losing a stable assignment: stability would imply uniqueness by the preceding homogeneous argument.  When the solution is unique, transposing (1) shows that \(P^{\mathsf T}\) is also a solution, so \(P=P^{\mathsf T}\).  Positive definiteness is then checked exactly by successive rational Schur complements.  Indeed, for
\[
 P=\begin{pmatrix}a&b^{\mathsf T}\\ b&D\end{pmatrix}
 \quad\text{with }a>0,
\]
completion of the square gives
\[
 \begin{pmatrix}s\\y\end{pmatrix}^{\!\mathsf T}
 P
 \begin{pmatrix}s\\y\end{pmatrix}
 =a\left(s+a^{-1}b^{\mathsf T}y\right)^2
  +y^{\mathsf T}\left(D-a^{-1}bb^{\mathsf T}\right)y.
\]
Thus \(P\) is positive definite exactly when \(a>0\) and the displayed Schur complement is positive definite; induction reduces the decision to exact signs of rational pivots.  A nonpositive or zero pivot is correctly rejected.  Finally, after denominators are cleared, every determinant used by elimination is a sum of at most \((c^2)!\) products of \(c^2\) input integers.  Its binary length is therefore polynomial in \(c\) and \(L\), and the same is true of all minors and rational pivots.  Normalization, solution of (1), and the sign tests consequently take \(\operatorname{poly}(c,L)\) bit operations per admissible matching.  This factor is already allowed in the preceding local bound, so retaining precisely the locally stable assignments has total screening time
\[
 \sum_{C\in\operatorname{SCC}(B)}
 O\!\left(\bigl(c^{1/2}e_C+cN_{\mathrm{adm}}(W_C)\bigr)
          \operatorname{poly}(c,L)\right).
\]

For each component, the preceding argument produces every member of \(\mathcal P_{\mathrm{stab}}(W_C)\) exactly once.  The already established \(\mathrm{thm:scc\mbox{-}factorization}\) says that restriction and concatenation in the fixed topological component order give a bijection
\[
 \prod_{C\in\operatorname{SCC}(B)}\mathcal P_{\mathrm{stab}}(W_C)
 \;\longrightarrow\;\mathcal P_{\mathrm{stab}}(W).
\]
A lexicographic mixed-radix counter visits every tuple in this Cartesian product exactly once.  Advancing the counter touches at most the number of components, and materializing the concatenated permutation writes exactly \(q\) entries; hence the delay per stable global assignment is \(O(q)\) after local screening.  The screening term contains \(N_{\mathrm{adm}}(W_C)\), including local matchings rejected by (2), so this argument makes no polynomial-delay assertion in \(N_{\mathrm{stab}}(W)\) alone.  This proves every part of the proposition.
